fixes.explanation: That's what Jesus says, friend. He tells them, “…not one stone will be left on another; every one will be thrown down.” The disciples were busy admiring the stonework, and I bet nobody saw that sentence coming. It's a heavy word, and I think it landed hard.

Gold is a fun guess, friend, but Jesus says nothing like that. The disciples are talking about beautiful stones and consecrated gifts, and He says the time will come when not one stone is left on another. Every one will be thrown down. No gold shows up anywhere in His answer.

Nope, the disciples don't ask who or how to stop it. They ask, “…when will these things happen? And what will be the sign that they are about to take place?” They want the timing and a warning sign. Asking how to stop it is a whole different question, friend.

That's the list. Jesus says, “There will be great earthquakes, famines, and pestilences in various places…” It's a heavy list, and He doesn't sugarcoat it. But He gave it to the disciples ahead of time, and I think that's a kindness.

Signs is the word. Jesus says there will be “…fearful sights and great signs from heaven.” Remember that the disciples asked about a sign. Signs are part of His answer, though He also warns them about people claiming, “The time is near,” and says, “Do not follow them.” (Luke 21:8)

Jesus doesn't say that, friend. He talks about adversaries and says He will give the disciples speech and wisdom that none of them will be able to resist or contradict. He tells them to make up their minds not to worry beforehand how to defend themselves. The words come from Him.

Servants and hired workers aren't on Jesus' list. He says, “You will be betrayed even by parents and brothers and relatives and friends…” Those are family and friends. It's a hard line, and I think it hurts to hear.

True. Right after the hard words, Jesus says, “Yet not even a hair of your head will perish.” That sits next to being hated and some being put to death. Those words come together in what He says to them.

A new star would be pretty to look at, but Jesus doesn't say that. He says, “But when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, you will know that her desolation is near.” The sign is armies around the city. It's a sober picture, friend.

Right. Jesus says, “For these are the days of vengeance, to fulfill all that is written.” That ties these days to what Scripture has already said. It's a heavy passage, friend. The purpose He names is fulfilling all that is written.

Jesus doesn't mention crowning anyone. He says, “For these are the days of vengeance, to fulfill all that is written.” The purpose He names is fulfilling what is written. It's a serious moment, friend.
